What is Cryptocurrency?

Cryptocurrency is digital money. You can't hold it in your hand like cash because it exists only on computers connected through the internet.

Unlike regular money that is managed by governments and banks, cryptocurrencies work through thousands of computers around the world. Every transaction is recorded on a blockchain.

Bitcoin was the first cryptocurrency, introduced in 2009. Today there are thousands of cryptocurrencies including Ethereum, Solana, Avalanche and many others.

Understanding cryptocurrency before investing helps you avoid scams, unrealistic expectations and expensive mistakes.

Regular Money Cryptocurrency
Controlled by a government and central bankControlled by a global network of computers
Bank insures deposits up to a limitNo government insurance on holdings
Mistaken payments can often be reversedTransactions are generally permanent
Bank can freeze or assist with your accountNo central authority to call for help

What is crypto trading?

01 — Investing

Buy and hold

Buying a cryptocurrency and holding onto it for months or years, hoping it becomes more valuable over time — closer to how people invest in stocks.

02 — Trading

Buy and sell frequently

Buying and selling more often — sometimes within days, hours, or minutes — trying to profit from short-term price changes. Most beginners who try this lose money.

In plain terms: Investing is generally slower and lower risk because you're holding assets for a longer period. Trading focuses on short-term price movements, requires more experience, and carries a higher chance of losing money if you don't have a proper strategy.

How does crypto trading actually work?

01

Create an account on an exchange

A digital marketplace where people buy and sell crypto, similar in idea to a stock market.

02

Verify your identity

Required by law on legitimate exchanges. If a platform skips this, treat it as a warning sign.

03

Deposit money

Transfer regular currency, like US dollars, into your exchange account.

04

Place an order

Choose which cryptocurrency to buy and how much. The exchange matches you with a seller.

05

Store it

It sits in the exchange's storage, or you move it to your own personal wallet.

06

Buy, hold, or sell

Based on your own research — never on pressure or promises of guaranteed profit.

The good side & the risks of crypto

Crypto has advantages, but it also carries real risks. Learn both before investing.

Risks

Price volatility

01

Crypto prices can rise or fall dramatically within hours.

Scams & fraud

02

Fake investment schemes and phishing attacks are common.

No guaranteed protection

03

Unlike bank deposits, crypto usually has no government insurance.

Irreversible transactions

04

Sending funds to the wrong address usually cannot be reversed.

Regulatory uncertainty

05

Rules and taxation vary by country and can change over time.

Private key loss

06

If you lose your recovery phrase, you may permanently lose access to your crypto.

Pros vs. Cons, Side by Side

Crypto has real advantages, but it also comes with real risks. Looking at both together helps you make better decisions.

Open to anyone, anytime

Remember: Crypto is neither completely good nor completely bad. Understanding both the opportunities and the risks will help you make informed decisions instead of emotional ones.

Crypto terms every beginner should know

You'll see these words everywhere in crypto. Understanding them early makes the rest of your learning much easier.

Wallet

A crypto wallet stores your digital assets and private keys. Some wallets are managed by exchanges, while self-custody wallets give you full control.

Seed Phrase

A 12–24 word recovery phrase used to restore your wallet. Anyone with these words can access your funds.

Important: Your seed phrase and private key should never be shared with anyone. Losing them may permanently lock you out of your crypto, while sharing them allows others to steal it.

How to Approach Crypto Safely

Learning crypto is much safer when you understand the basics first. These practical guidelines can help reduce common mistakes and improve your confidence before making financial decisions.

01

Learn Before You Buy

Understand what Bitcoin, Ethereum, wallets, and blockchain actually do before investing any money.

02

Only Invest What You Can Lose

Never use emergency savings, borrowed money, or rent money for crypto investments.

03

Start Small

Begin with a small amount while learning instead of chasing huge profits immediately.

04

Choose Trusted Exchanges

Use well-known, regulated exchanges that provide strong security and customer support.

05

Enable Two-Factor Authentication

Protect every crypto account using 2FA to reduce the risk of unauthorized access.

06

Protect Your Seed Phrase

Never share your recovery phrase. Store it offline in a secure location.

07

Ignore Hype & FOMO

Don't buy simply because everyone on social media is talking about a coin.

08

Think Long Term

Successful investing usually comes from patience, research, and disciplined decisions.

Knowledge is Your Best Investment

The safest crypto strategy isn't finding the next coin—it's learning how the technology works, understanding the risks, and making informed decisions without fear or hype.
